AWS CloudFormation is a service that manages the infrastructure through code 
(AWS, n.d.), and in the context of the project, defined in the CDK. By defining 
the resources and their dependencies, CloudFormation handles the provision and 
configuration process. 
A stack within CloudFormation is a collection of services and resources that are 
bundled into a single unit, similar to an object within OOP (AWS, n.d.). All 
resources within a stack are defined, managed, and updated as a single unit; 
this modular approach allows for small parts of the backend to be changed 
without the need to re-provision the entire project. 
In Figure 49, a modified class diagram delineates the classes within the CDK. 
The diagram takes a pragmatic and unique approach while depicting the classes 
with the inclusion of an “*”, highlighting local variables within stacks that are of 
importance. This employed strategy ensures that the reader understands where 
certain parts of the infrastructure are defined. 
The ApplicationStage as highlighted in Figure 49 is a part of the deployment 
pipeline. A stage in this sense, is essentially a repeatable unit that defines the 
entire projects infrastructure, thus multiple stages can be created for testing and 
production. 
The ApplicationStage defines all the stacks required: 
- VirtualPrivateCloudStack: Defines the virtual private cloud configuration 
where the projects resources will be. 
- StorageStack: Where all tables and S3 buckets are defined, including the 
code bucket that stores the Lambda’s code. 
- CognitoStack: Defines all user authentication through AWS Cognito. 
- ECSStack: Manages the ECS, load balancing, and DNS configuration for 
HTTPS integration.
